question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: **Are on a collision course**

options.text: Moving towards each other in a peaceful way
Having different goals but no conflict

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Heading towards an inevitable conflict .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "Are on a collision course" implies that two entities (individuals, groups, or organizations) are heading towards a situation where conflict or disagreement is inevitable.
 
• This expression is typically used to describe scenarios where there are opposing views, interests, or actions, leading to a clash.
 
• Among the given options, option 1, "Heading towards an inevitable conflict," best captures the meaning of this idiom.

Correct interpretation: *The idiom "Are on a collision course" signifies that two parties are moving towards a conflict or disagreement that cannot be avoided.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Example Usage:**
 
 
• After the heated argument during the meeting, both departments are on a collision course regarding budget allocation.
 
• With their vastly different political ideologies, the two candidates are on a collision course for the upcoming debate.
 
 
 
• **Common Contexts:**
 
 
• Used in personal, professional, or political contexts to describe impending conflicts.
 
• Highlights situations where reconciliation or resolution seems unlikely.
